inputs.text: This wasn’t just a paperwork error. People showed up in immigration court seeking legal status, and ICE lawyers used a memo to justify arresting and detaining thousands—now prosecutors say it didn’t even authorize those arrests. That reversal looks less like accountability than a controlled retreat: the system used legal language to turn court attendance into a trap, then backed away from the memo once it became harder to defend. The real question is who decided this was acceptable, and how long they thought the cover story would work.
